questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.text: The value of k for which the pair of equations kx = y + 2 and 6x = 2y + 3 has infinitely many solutions,
questions.solution: Write them as kx − y − 2 = 0 and 6x − 2y − 3 = 0. Infinitely many solutions need k/6 = (−1)/(−2) = (−2)/(−3), i.e. k/6 = 1/2 = 2/3. Since 1/2 ≠ 2/3, no such k exists.

questions.text: In what ratio, does x-axis divide the line segment joining the points A(3, 6) and B(−12, −3) ?
questions.solution: Let the ratio be k : 1. On the x-axis y = 0, so (−3k + 6)/(k + 1) = 0 and k = 2. The ratio is 2 : 1.

questions.text: The least positive value of k, for which the quadratic equation 2x² + kx − 4 = 0 has rational roots, is
questions.solution: Rational roots need D = k² + 32 to be a perfect square. k = 1 gives 33 (no), k = 2 gives 36 = 6² (yes). So the least positive value is k = 2.

questions.text: Which of the following is a quadratic polynomial having zeroes −2/3 and 2/3 ?
questions.solution: Sum of zeroes = 0 and product = −4/9, so the polynomial is k(x² − 4/9), i.e. a multiple of 9x² − 4. Only 5(9x² − 4) fits.

questions.text: A girl calculates that the probability of her winning the first prize in a lottery is 0.08. If 6000 tickets are sold, how many tickets has she bought ?
questions.solution: Tickets bought = 0.08 × 6000 = 480.

questions.text: In a group of 20 people, 5 can't swim. If one person is selected at random, then the probability that he/she can swim, is
questions.solution: 15 of the 20 people can swim, so P = 15/20 = 3/4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Point P(0, 2) is the point of intersection of y-axis with the line 3x + 2y = 4.
Reason (R): The distance of point P(0, 2) from x-axis is 2 units.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Putting x = 0 in 3x + 2y = 4 gives y = 2, so A is true. P(0, 2) is 2 units from the x-axis, so R is true, but that does not explain where the line meets the y-axis.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.text: Solve the pair of equations x = 3 and y = −4 graphically.
questions.solution: x = 3 is a vertical line through (3, 0) and y = −4 is a horizontal line through (0, −4). They meet at (3, −4), so x = 3, y = −4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.text: Using graphical method, find whether following system of linear equations is consistent or not : x = 0 and y = −7
questions.solution: x = 0 is the y-axis and y = −7 is a horizontal line through (0, −7). They intersect at exactly one point, (0, −7), so the system is consistent with a unique solution.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If sin α = 1/√2 and cot β = √3, then find the value of cosec α + cosec β.
questions.solution: sin α = 1/√2 gives cosec α = √2. cot β = √3 gives β = 30°, so cosec β = 2. cosec α + cosec β = √2 + 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the greatest number which divides 85 and 72 leaving remainders 1 and 2 respectively.
questions.solution: The number divides 85 − 1 = 84 and 72 − 2 = 70 exactly. 84 = 2² × 3 × 7 and 70 = 2 × 5 × 7, so HCF = 2 × 7 = 14. The greatest such number is 14.

questions.text: A bag contains 4 red, 3 blue and 2 yellow balls. One ball is drawn at random from the bag. Find the probability that drawn ball is (i) red (ii) yellow.
questions.solution: There are 9 balls. (i) P(red) = 4/9. (ii) P(yellow) = 2/9.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.text: Half of the difference between two numbers is 2. The sum of the greater number and twice the smaller number is 13. Find the numbers.
questions.solution: Let the greater number be x and the smaller y. (x − y)/2 = 2 gives x − y = 4, and x + 2y = 13. Subtracting: 3y = 9, so y = 3 and x = 7. The numbers are 7 and 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Prove that √5 is an irrational number.
questions.solution: Assume √5 = a/b with a, b coprime integers, b ≠ 0. Then a² = 5b², so 5 divides a², hence 5 divides a. Write a = 5c: 25c² = 5b², so b² = 5c² and 5 divides b. Then 5 divides both a and b, contradicting that they are coprime. So √5 is irrational.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If (−5, 3) and (5, 3) are two vertices of an equilateral triangle, then find co-ordinates of the third vertex, given that origin lies inside the triangle. (Take √3 = 1.7)
questions.solution: The side is 10 and the third vertex lies on the perpendicular bisector x = 0, at a distance of (√3/2) × 10 = 5√3 from (0, 3). Since the origin is inside, the vertex is below: (0, 3 − 5√3) = (0, 3 − 8.5) = (0, −5.5).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn to a circle with centre O from an external point T. Prove that ∠PTQ = 2∠OPQ.
questions.solution: TP = TQ, so Δ TPQ is isosceles and ∠TPQ = ∠TQP = (180° − ∠PTQ)/2 = 90° − ½∠PTQ. The radius is perpendicular to the tangent, so ∠OPT = 90°. Then ∠OPQ = 90° − ∠TPQ = ½∠PTQ, i.e. ∠PTQ = 2∠OPQ.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Prove that : (tan θ + sec θ − 1)/(tan θ − sec θ + 1) = (1 + sin θ)/cos θ
questions.solution: In the numerator replace 1 by sec²θ − tan²θ: tan θ + sec θ − (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = (tan θ + sec θ)(1 − sec θ + tan θ). The second factor equals the denominator, so the fraction = tan θ + sec θ = sin θ/cos θ + 1/cos θ = (1 + sin θ)/cos θ.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A room is in the form of cylinder surmounted by a hemi-spherical dome. The base radius of hemisphere is one-half the height of cylindrical part. Find total height of the room if it contains (1408/21) m³ of air. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution: Let the radius be r, so the cylinder's height is 2r. Volume = πr²(2r) + (2/3)πr³ = (8/3)πr³ = (176/21)r³ = 1408/21, so r³ = 8 and r = 2 m. Total height = 2r + r = 6 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: An empty cone is of radius 3 cm and height 12 cm. Ice-cream is filled in it so that lower part of the cone which is (1/6)th of the volume of the cone is unfilled but hemisphere is formed on the top. Find volume of the ice-cream. (Take π = 3.14)
questions.solution: Volume of cone = (1/3)π × 9 × 12 = 36π. Filled part of the cone = (5/6) × 36π = 30π. Hemisphere on top = (2/3)π × 27 = 18π. Ice-cream = 48π = 48 × 3.14 = 150.72 cm³.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides at distinct points, prove that the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.
questions.solution: Let DE ∥ BC in ΔABC, with D on AB and E on AC. Join BE and CD, and draw EN ⊥ AB and DM ⊥ AC. ar(ADE)/ar(BDE) = (½ × AD × EN)/(½ × DB × EN) = AD/DB, and ar(ADE)/ar(DEC) = AE/EC. ΔBDE and ΔDEC are on the same base DE and between the same parallels DE and BC, so their areas are equal. Hence AD/DB = AE/EC.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower 24 m high from the foot of another tower in the same plane is 60°. The angle of elevation of the top of second tower from the foot of the first tower is 30°. Find the distance between two towers and the height of the other tower. Also, find the length of the wire attached to the tops of both the towers.
questions.solution: Let the distance be d. tan 60° = 24/d, so d = 24/√3 = 8√3 m. The second tower's height h = d tan 30° = 8√3 × 1/√3 = 8 m. The wire joins the tops: horizontal gap 8√3 m, vertical gap 24 − 8 = 16 m, so its length = √(192 + 256) = √448 = 8√7 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A spherical balloon of radius r subtends an angle of 60° at the eye of an observer. If the angle of elevation of its centre is 45° from the same point, then prove that height of the centre of the balloon is √2 times its radius.
questions.solution: Let E be the eye and C the centre. The tangents from E to the balloon make an angle of 60°, so each makes 30° with EC, and the radius to a point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent. So sin 30° = r/EC, giving EC = 2r. The height of the centre = EC sin 45° = 2r × 1/√2 = √2 r.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A chord of a circle of radius 14 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the area of the corresponding minor segment of the circle. Also find the area of the major segment of the circle.
questions.solution: Sector = (60/360) × (22/7) × 14² = 308/3 ≈ 102.67 cm². The chord makes an equilateral triangle of area (√3/4) × 14² = 49√3 ≈ 84.87 cm² (√3 = 1.732). Minor segment ≈ 102.67 − 84.87 = 17.80 cm². Circle area = (22/7) × 196 = 616 cm², so major segment ≈ 616 − 17.80 = 598.20 cm².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: 250 logs are stacked in the following manner : 22 logs in the bottom row, 21 in the next row, 20 in the row next to it and so on. In how many rows, are the 250 logs placed and how many logs are there in the top row ?
questions.solution: a = 22, d = −1. Sₙ = (n/2)[44 − (n − 1)] = 250 gives n(45 − n) = 500, i.e. n² − 45n + 500 = 0, so (n − 20)(n − 25) = 0. n = 25 would make the top row 22 − 24 = −2, which is impossible, so n = 20. Top row = 22 − 19 = 3 logs.

questions.text:
While designing the school year book, a teacher asked the student that the length and width of a particular photo is increased by x units each to double the area of the photo. The original photo is 18 cm long and 12 cm wide.

Write an algebraic equation depicting the above information.
questions.solution: New area = twice the old area: (18 + x)(12 + x) = 2 × 18 × 12 = 432.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
While designing the school year book, a teacher asked the student that the length and width of a particular photo is increased by x units each to double the area of the photo. The original photo is 18 cm long and 12 cm wide.

What should be the new dimensions of the enlarged photo ?
questions.solution: x² + 30x − 216 = 0 factorises as (x + 36)(x − 6) = 0, so x = 6. The new photo is 24 cm long and 18 cm wide.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
While designing the school year book, a teacher asked the student that the length and width of a particular photo is increased by x units each. The original photo is 18 cm long and 12 cm wide.

Can any rational value of x make the new area equal to 220 cm² ?
questions.solution: (18 + x)(12 + x) = 220 gives x² + 30x − 4 = 0. D = 900 + 16 = 916, which is not a perfect square, so x is irrational. No rational value of x works.

questions.text:
India meteorological department observes seasonal and annual rainfall every year in different sub-divisions of our country. The table given below shows sub-division wise seasonal (monsoon) rainfall (mm) in 2018 :

1000 – 1200 : 2

questions.solution: The highest frequency is 7, in the class 600 – 800.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
The table below shows sub-division wise seasonal (monsoon) rainfall (mm) in 2018 :

Rainfall (mm) : Number of Sub-divisions
200 – 400 : 2
400 – 600 : 4
600 – 800 : 7
800 – 1000 : 4
1000 – 1200 : 2
1200 – 1400 : 3
1400 – 1600 : 1
1600 – 1800 : 1

Find the median of the given data.
questions.solution: N = 24, N/2 = 12. Cumulative frequencies: 2, 6, 13, … so the median class is 600 – 800 with l = 600, cf = 6, f = 7, h = 200. Median = 600 + ((12 − 6)/7) × 200 = 600 + 171.43 ≈ 771.43 mm.
